subject: Prioritize Public Transit
comment: Dear council, Please increase our contribution to the UTA in the next budget. The UTA desperately needs more funding to improve service. While I appreciate the efforts the city is making on walkability and bikeability, the missing piece for the SLC metro is public transit. For people that live in St County that are commuting into SLC, public transit is not a viable option for them to get to work. If they all continue to commute via private vehicles, one of two things, if not both is going to happen: 1) We're going to have to continue to build an auto-oriented city to accommodate them. This means more motor vehicle fatalities, more obesity and its associated helath issues, worse traffic, more Amazon warehouse deliveries because people don't run errands on foot, and longer commute times. Reserving so much scarce space for cars also decreases housing affordability because they take up so much space. 2) Businesses are going to choose to locate away from the downtown core and likely outside of SLC altogether which will substantially reduce our long-term productivity and the availability of high-quality jobs for our residents. When businesses tell us that they need more parking for their downtown offices, I understand why they are saying this and they're not wrong. As long as their employees that live outside of SLC have to commute via car, they need somewhere to park. It would not surprise me at all if businesses start to say that it's just not worth it to locate downtown. I realize it would be nice if the state funded the UTA to appropriate levels but it won't. So we have to step in and fund the UTA to get the higher level of service we need to meet all of our Plan Salt Lake goals. We're at a critical tipping point with our city. We're adding density but, right now, public transit is still not a competitive option for a lot of residents in the city for some trips and, outside of the city, it's not competitive at all. Free fares are great but the main cost of taking transit for the vast majority of our citizens is that it takes so much longer than driving right now. That has to change and that takes money.

comment: Ana and Chris-I will write the other members of the Council and plan to speak AGAIN on Tuesday night. My comment from the hearing on Downtown Building Heights on 4/18 is below. It took a while to get confirmation of what Jack Davis has written and what I suspected. This proposal regarding building heights will apply CITYWIDE. The FBUN-2 zone applies CITYWIDE and has been used in Central City twice. The projects have not been constructed. So I can't point to how bad the results are...yet. The Council is looking at a map which does NOT reflect the impact of the proposed changes. I have copied Merrilee and David in District 3 because I think it is very possible that the FBUN-2 could be applied there in the future. Two large parcels in the Central City Historic District have already been zoned FBUN-2. A member of the City Council has acknowledged publicly that the FBUN-2 has problems and done nothing. The zone never should have been applied in an historic district without additional restrictions. Now you are looking in one place and ready to make changes which will affect other neighborhoods. This is similar to the error that the City made when adopting the FBUN-2 CITYWIDE after only studying it in Central Ninth. I have boundless energy but not boundless patience. Relentlessly, cindy c. April 18, 2023 comment: I am stuck in my own version of the movie Groundhog Day, doomed to complain about the same issues over and over again, until someday my complaint is viewed as precisely correct by at least 4 members of the City Council. About 7 years ago, I teamed up with an architect, planner, and attorney to deal with the FBUN-2 zone. It had been applied City-wide after being studied only in the Central 9th area. We had to engage the State Ombudsman for Property Rights and get the assistance of Judi Short regarding setpbacks because the zone had none unless it was next to FBUN-1. AND the use of the FBUN-2 was adopted City-wide and then proposed in the Central City Historic District. The FBUN-2 is a blank check for developers and is inappropriate for use in historic districts with lower density zoning without additional limitations. That is precisely where the City has applied it...south of Trolley Square and at the Western Gardens site...where the blocks are two of the finest collections of contributory structures in the Central City Historic District. I cannot find any information in the packet which gives me confidence that the City is not making the same mistake again...failing to consider the consequences of using the FBUN-2 outside the area for which it was designed. It was never intended for use in historic district, but the City has now mapped it in the Central City District repeatedly. The map you have focuses exclusively on the Downtown area. I think the proposed changes will apply more broadly and will include Central City and other low to medium density neighborhoods where additional height is not appropriate such as Capitol Hill and the southwest portion of the Avenues. #1 I am asking you to keep the public hearing open. #2 Please restrict any changes to the area covered by the map in your packet. I do not believe that the consequences elsewhere have been considered. #3 Finally, if this ordinance is too complicated for me to figure out, maybe, just maybe, it is too complicated. Just tell developers that if they want additional height, they have to include affordable housing.

subject: Cut police budget, spend on housing first initiatives
comment: Homelessness is a huge problem in SLC. Housing First initiatives in other regions have proven effective at ending homelessness, AND cost less than policing homelessness. The city should cut the SLC police budget and use the money to invest in housing and legal homeless camps. That will be more effective than having police do sweeps.

subject: City Budget Hearings
comment: Feedback: More Traffic cops?: I witness an amazing number of speeders and people who run red lights. I was taught in Germany that an orange light means slow down instead of speed up. Emphasis on Open Space?: I am spoiled. I am from Boulder, Colorado. I didn't have to drive to the mountains for open space. It can also be utilized as bicycle corridors. Sidewalks/ Mass transit?: I am confused. I'd love to know why so many of the new construction projects are built so close to the road that the width of the sidewalks are minimal. And the small sidewalks are located right next to the traffic with no buffer and no room for trees. How do you create a walkable/ rideable community with tiny sidewalks? Check out some of the Euro cities. Munich has awesome paths for bikes and pedestrians. Thanks for the opportunity for giving feedback.

subject: Public Hearings May 16, June 6 2023
comment: Tom whom it concerns: How is it the city lets large contractors not pay impact fees? While you are allowing unprecedented urban construction growth in Salt Lake City, our roads have become obstacle courses, and heavy duty shock absorbers are required to navigate surface streets. You have made the ridiculous decision to narrow streets, especially South Temple. Why? It impedes traffic and it is my suspicion that you have caved to the complaints of the neighbors on that street. You need to keep the brown can pickup year around. Branches and leaves don't stop falling and blowing just because it's winter. If you want to stop the service, then reimburse your customers for the time it is unavailable to them. The police department does NOT need to be defunded ! I like having the police keeping crime at bay. Stop even talking about defunding the police! Ron McCormick

subject: budget comments
comment: Hello, I am responding to the mailer you sent out regarding budget planning. Here are my top priorities for the future of SLC: 1. SLC PD budget. We need to raise Officers pay so we don't lose them to other cities, which is what is currently happening. Living in the Ballpark and working in Sugarhouse, I use law enforcement almost every day. 2. Increase jail size. What is the point of arresting criminals if they are out the same night. This happens all the time. It is very frustrating. 3. Homeless services. It is time to get people off the streets and get them the help they need to work on mental health, addiction, and joblessness. 4. Infrastructure and parks. Our city is growing so fast. We need to continue to focus on the bones to ensure future growth can be accommodated. Side note- are they ever going to finish 300W? I would also say garbage clean up from the homeless. My part of the city is dirty. Very dirty. It is not always a city I am proud of and that should change. Thanks,Bryson Thomas

subject: City Budget
comment: To whom it may concern, I think with the highway expansion and remodeling set to release later this year that the tax money should go towards supporting and working with that new design. Also of course, possibility unrelated but supporting those homes that may become displaced by the expansion would also be a important focus with the major Project release this year. Thanks, Krista Flavin

subject: Homeless Shelters
comment: I recently saw in the news that there are plans to begin work to place homeless shelters throughout our neighborhoods. While I am compassionate to people less fortunate than myself I do not want the problems associated with homeless shelter(s) in our neighborhood. We work very hard to buy homes and maintain them so that we have a pleasant community. The situations of vagrants, filth, loitering, theft, breaking and entering as well as indecent exposure and public urination and defecation have all gotten worse since rio grande was cleared out. I for one want the homeless town on Rio grande re-established. We do not want what has been done in so many other formerly beautiful cites done here. I had a man defecate on my back porch last summer and attempt to set up camp in my back yard. This is dangerous to everyone involved, and I work too hard to tolerate it for one minute. Put the shelters down town where it was before, and focus on cleaning our parks and neighborhoods back up. While many people can recover from homelessness, many cannot for physical and mental health reasons, combined with drug addiction. WE DO NOT WANT THESE ELEMENTS ADJACENT TO OUR HOMES. We do not want salt lake to become the next San Francisco. Please converse with the mayor, and re-evaluate course. The people of Salt Lake do not approve.
